notes.3a: The difference between the two areas was used correctly by most candidates to show that x -10x – 24 = 0. Those who expanded (x+5) usually did so correctly. The most common errors were to start with the difference the wrong way round or to miss the =0 at some stage. A few started with x -10x + 24 =0 and tried to factorise it.
notes.3b: This was well answered by the majority of candidates - even those who had not been successful in part (a) . Most factorised correctly but a few used the formula, which was fine if they used it correctly. Some failed to relate the equation back to the initial problem so incorrectly included -2 as a possible value of x.
notes.3c: This part caused more problems than the rest of the question. Some found the correct angle but it was very rare to see the most efficient method being used. There were numerous incorrect answers of 26.6° where candidates did not recognise that they needed to double this angle. Most candidates tended to use a combination of Pythagoras’ theorem, sine rule and cosine rule. This often resulted in errors being made. 56 Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0580 Mathematics June 2011

notes.5bi: This part of the question was generally well answered. Some candidates drew the perpendicular bisector in the correct position but failed to show the two pairs of arcs which meant that only one mark was earned. It is important that candidates understand that they must not erase their construction arcs after the perpendicular bisector has been located.
notes.5bii: This was also well answered. The candidates who failed to score any marks in this part of the question had mostly constructed the perpendicular bisector of the line BC . ( c) Those candidates who drew the correct bisectors in part (b) , usually went on to score both of the marks in part (c) . However, some candidates did not measure the distance of Q from AB accurately and a common incorrect measurement was 2.3 cm.
notes.5biii: The table was completed successfully by most candidates and most completed the histogram correctly.
